title: Leigh air disaster
summary: A Blériot 155 aircraft operating a Paris to Croydon service encountered a fire in the port upper engine at 3:27 pm GMT while cruising. The fire spread to the wing and the aircraft changed direction toward Penshurst Airfield. The tail sank while the aircraft gained brief height, then rolled over and dived to the ground where it burned. This was the first recorded in-flight fire on an airliner.
probable_cause: In-flight fire in port upper engine that spread to the wing, causing loss of control.

factors.evidence: the port upper engine on fire and the fire was seen to spread to the wing
Then the aircraft rolled over and dived to the ground
the wreckage was consumed by fire and a petrol tank exploded

events.text: The aircraft departed Le Bourget Airport, Paris at 1:30 pm local time (12:30 pm GMT) bound for Croydon Airport.
At 3:24 pm GMT, the pilot radioed ahead to Croydon OK, passing over Tonbridge. All well.
At 3:27 pm, eyewitnesses reported seeing the aircraft with the port upper engine on fire; the fire was seen to spread to the wing.
Then the aircraft rolled over and dived to the ground where the wreckage was consumed by fire in the grounds of Southwood, Leigh, Kent.
